commands.review_summary:
The branch adds loopback checks to the trusted-host SSRF resolved-address guard, updates mocked SSRF regression tests, and also changes cron `--session` normalization behavior and tests.

PR surface: Source +15, Tests +48. Total +63 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source inspection: current main promotes matching `allowedOrigins` into `allowedHostnames`, then the trusted-host DNS-answer guard checks link-local and metadata addresses but not loopback. I did not run a live repro in this read-only external PR review.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual review is appropriate because this is an external SSRF-boundary PR with mock-only proof and unrelated CLI churn.

target.title: fix(ssrf): block loopback addresses for trusted hostname origins
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When resolving a host, if it matches one of the user-configured `allowedOrigins` (or `allowedHostnames`), the SSRF policy sets `skipPrivateNetworkChecks` to `true` to permit connection to local private network addresses.

This bypasses `assertAllowedResolvedAddressesOrThrow` in favor of `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow`. However, the latter was only checking for link-local and cloud metadata IP addresses. It completely omitted checks for loopback addresses (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`).

This is a security vulnerability: if a trusted private hostname or local-origin resolves/rebinds to a loopback address, the gateway will connect to localhost services, exposing the machine to DNS rebinding attacks targeting loopback-only APIs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added an explicit check for loopback IP addresses (`isLoopbackIpAddress`) inside `assertAllowedTrustedHostnameResolvedAddressesOrThrow` in `src/plugin-sdk/ssrf-policy.ts` so loopback addresses are blocked even for trusted origins, aligning with the SSRF policy requirement: "SSRF IP checks must block untrusted hostnames resolving/rebinding to loopback IP addresses (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`) unless the hostname is explicitly allowed by policy (such as `localhost` or local mock servers)."

## User Impact

Prevents DNS rebinding attacks targeting local loopback services, enhancing system boundary security.

## Evidence

Added unit tests in `src/plugin-sdk/ssrf-policy.test.ts` verifying that rebinding a trusted private origin to an IPv4/IPv6 loopback address is rejected. All 47 tests passed.
```
✓ |plugin-sdk| src/plugin-sdk/ssrf-policy.test.ts (47 tests) 38ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  47 passed (47)
```

### Real Behavior Proof

Running SSRF checks with a mock DNS lookup:
```
stdout | blocks trusted private hostname rebinding to loopback
=== Malicious Rebinding to Loopback ===
Status: Blocked successfully!
Error Message: Blocked: resolves to private/internal/special-use IP address
======================================

stdout | explicit localhost hostname still works
=== Explicit Localhost Allowed ===
Resolved IP: 127.0.0.1
==================================
```
